qolFindings.title: After Esci, a refresh that was already retrying still exchanges account 1's refresh token once the signal returns
qolFindings.evidence: Scratch run on 12d9171 (late2.spec.ts, fake backend, synthetic uno@example.test). Offline with an expired token, Esci tapped as the auto-refresh ticker began a retry series, token endpoint answering from +5 s. Log: '0.1 TOKEN aborted', '0.5', '1.4', '3.0', '3.6 FORM_SHOWN stored=false', '5.0 SIGNAL_BACK', '6.2 TOKEN ok'. Sampled each second for 30 s: the stored session stayed absent and the UI stayed on the form; after a reload still signed out. The device is not affected and SP-B3-2 holds, but the server issues a fresh session for a phone that just signed out, which adds to BACKLOG SP-B3-7 (local sign-out never revokes on the server).
qolFindings.reproduction: late2.spec.ts: sign in, switch, expire the token and abort /auth/v1/token, reload, wait for the launch retries to stop, tap Esci at the next ticker TOKEN request, open /auth/v1/token at +5 s, sample localStorage and the UI for 30 s, reload.

qolFindings.title: Offline with an expired token, the launch stays 'checking' for about 25 s
qolFindings.evidence: startBackupAtLaunch awaits auth.initialize(); with an expired stored session and no signal, initialize runs auth-js's refresh retry series (about 26 s) before the state leaves 'checking'. b3-backup-ui 'offline the morning after' took 40.8 s. No privacy impact; 'checking' hides the sign-in form. Passed on to field UX.
